families.name: Gradient-Based Attribution
families.definition: Methods that compute the gradient of the output score with respect to the input to identify influential features.

properties.text: These methods interpret the gradient as a sensitivity map indicating which pixels or features strongly influence the decision.
SmoothGrad improves visual sharpness by averaging gradients over multiple noisy inputs to remove noise.
Integrated Gradients satisfies axioms of Sensitivity and Implementation Invariance by integrating gradients along a path from a baseline to the input.
Grad-CAM uses gradients flowing into the final convolutional layer to produce coarse localization maps for target concepts.
Layer-Wise Relevance Propagation decomposes classification decisions by pixel-wise relevance propagation through the network layers.

limitations.text: Basic gradient maps can be noisy and require elaboration techniques like smoothing to be visually useful.
Most known attribution methods fail to satisfy fundamental axioms such as Sensitivity and Implementation Invariance.
These methods provide local explanations for specific inputs but do not necessarily explain the global behavior of the model.

families.name: Perturbation and Occlusion
families.definition: Techniques that explain predictions by observing how model outputs change when input features are perturbed, occluded, or replaced.

properties.text: LIME explains predictions by learning an interpretable surrogate model in the local neighborhood of the prediction.
DeepLIFT decomposes output predictions by backpropagating the difference between neuron activations and reference activations.
Flip points are identified as inputs on the boundary between output classes to interpret network decisions.
Adversarial evaluation schemes insert distracting sentences to test if reading comprehension systems truly understand language.

limitations.text: LIME and similar local surrogate methods do not scale to explaining entire datasets.
These methods often cannot correct the problems they reveal, such as models being right for the wrong reasons.
Adversarial evaluation can be defeated by constructing new loss functions, making detection of true understanding difficult.

families.name: Representation Analysis and Visualization
families.definition: Approaches that inspect internal network activations or synthesize inputs to understand what features the network has learned.

properties.text: Network Dissection quantifies interpretability by scoring the alignment between hidden units and semantic concepts like objects or textures.
Activation maximization synthesizes preferred inputs for neurons to visualize what each unit detects.
Saliency maps are used to understand what deep reinforcement learning agents attend to and how their policies evolve.
Analysis of DQNs reveals that learned features aggregate the state space in a hierarchical fashion.
Object detectors emerge in deep scene CNNs trained on scene classification, revealing internal object representations.

limitations.text: There is no clear understanding of why deep networks perform well or how they might be improved based solely on visualization.
Interpretability is often an axis of trade-off, where high discrimination power comes at the cost of low interpretability.
It is unclear whether individual high-level units have distinct meanings or if it is the space of units that matters.

families.name: Disentangled and Structured Representations
families.definition: Architectures or training objectives designed to learn representations where factors of variation are encoded independently or in structured forms.

properties.text: InfoGAN maximizes mutual information between latent variables and observations to learn disentangled representations unsupervised.
Capsules use activity vectors to represent instantiation parameters of entities, with length indicating existence probability.
Gradient-isolated learning splits networks into modules trained to preserve input information without end-to-end backpropagation.
Contrastive Predictive Coding learns representations by predicting the future in latent space using autoregressive models.
Part graphs embed object-part concepts into CNNs to create semantically interpretable graphical models.

limitations.text: There is little empirical evidence that disentangled representations are more suitable for abstract reasoning tasks.
Biological-inspired methods like gradient isolation rely on greedy training which may not optimize global performance.
Disentangled representations are often argued to be useful but lack rigorous proof of their benefit for downstream tasks.

families.name: Adversarial Robustness and Detection
families.definition: Methods aimed at understanding, detecting, or mitigating the vulnerability of neural networks to adversarial examples.

properties.text: Adversarial examples are inputs with small perturbations that cause high-confidence misclassification.
Virtual Adversarial Training uses local smoothness of the conditional label distribution as a regularization method.
Robust optimization provides a unifying view on adversarial robustness by treating it as a minimax problem.
Adversarial patches are universal, robust, and targeted perturbations that can fool classifiers in the real world.
One-pixel attacks use differential evolution to generate minimal perturbations that fool networks in a black-box setting.

limitations.text: Adversarial examples are significantly harder to detect than previously appreciated, with ten detection methods being defeated.
The existence of adversarial attacks may be an inherent weakness of deep learning models due to their linear nature.
Cross-entropy loss and low-rank features are responsible for the existence of adversarial examples, requiring rethinking of loss functions.

families.name: Interpretable Model Architectures
families.definition: Model designs that inherently provide transparency or verifiability, such as decision trees or attention mechanisms.

properties.text: VIPER trains decision tree policies that are nonparametric and can be efficiently verified using existing techniques.
Attention mechanisms, such as bottom-up and top-down attention, allow models to focus on specific image regions or source words.
Residual Attention Networks incorporate attention modules to generate attention-aware features in an end-to-end fashion.
Adaptive attention models decide whether to use visual information at each time step, improving efficiency and interpretability.

limitations.text: Decision tree policies are difficult to train despite their verifiability.
Attention mechanisms may not always align with human attention, as shown by discrepancies in VQA tasks.
Interpretable models may sacrifice accuracy for interpretability, creating a trade-off.
There is very little consensus on what interpretable machine learning is and how it should be measured.
It remains unclear to what extent reading comprehension systems truly understand language versus relying on superficial patterns.
The real-world applicability of deep reinforcement learning is limited by the inability to ensure the safety of learned policies.
It is not well understood how to explain the strategies used by deep reinforcement learning agents to maximize rewards.
There is a lack of empirical evidence supporting the claim that disentangled representations are useful for solving real-world downstream tasks.
Adversarial examples are difficult to detect, and the properties believed to be intrinsic to them are not actually intrinsic.
The transition of features from general to specific in deep neural networks has not been studied extensively.
